    Six ideas, one question

    Each generation of model reads text a bit more like a person. Tap a rung to see what it does and how it scored on the same test.

    Where it still fails

    A fair result shows the misses too.

    1 of 94

    Posts about miscellaneous religion that our best model found. A blind guesser finds about 5. Those forums discuss the same things, so the topics blur.

    Lost "not"

    Our cleaning deletes small words. "I don't believe in any god" becomes "believe god arguments religion convince". It still got this right, but cleaning has a cost.

    How it works

    1. Clean

    Lowercase, then remove punctuation, numbers and common small words.

    2. Weigh

    Rare, telling words such as "pitcher" count for more than common ones.

    3. Score

    A trained model turns the weights into a percentage for each of the 20 topics.

    Data and setup

    20 Newsgroups with headers, footers and quotes removed. Stratified 70/15/15 split, seed 42: 13,192 train, 2,827 validation, 2,827 test. The tester on this page is a linear model on TF-IDF (10,000 words), 71.1% on the test set. Fine-tuned BERT (bert-base-uncased, 3 epochs, 2e-5, 256 tokens) reached 71.5% but needs a server, so it is not run here.

    Honest limits

    One run per model, so gaps under about 2 points are not conclusive. The 500-post language-model sample has a margin near 4 points. Short typed sentences differ from the long posts the model learned from, so expect lower confidence.

    Built from a university NLP assignment. Results come from our own experiments.
